message.content:
**Killing VS Code (code.exe) from the command line**

On Windows you can terminate a running program with the built‑in `taskkill` utility.  
Below are the most common ways to stop **VS Code** (`code.exe`) safely.

---

### 1. Kill *all* VS Code windows at once

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM` – specifies the image name (process name).  
* `/F` – forces termination (equivalent to “End Task” in Task Manager).

This will close every instance of `code.exe` that is currently running.

---

### 2. Kill a *specific* VS Code window

If you only want to close one particular window, first find its PID:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

You’ll see output similar to:

```
Image Name                     PID Session Name        Session#    Mem Usage
========================= ======== ================ =========== ============
code.exe                    12345 Console                    1     50,000 K
```

Then kill that specific PID:

```cmd
taskkill /PID 12345 /F
```

Replace `12345` with the actual PID you obtained.

---

### 3. Using PowerShell (alternative)

If you prefer PowerShell, the equivalent command is:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or for a specific PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id 12345 -Force
```

---

### Things to keep in mind

| ⚠️ | Note |
|---|------|
| 1 | `taskkill /F` forces the process to quit immediately. Any unsaved work in VS Code will be lost. |
| 2 | If you’re running VS Code as an administrator, you may need to run the command prompt itself as an administrator to kill it. |
| 3 | Use `tasklist` first to double‑check you’re targeting the right process. |
| 4 | On some systems, `code.exe` may be launched under a different name (e.g., `Code.exe`). Adjust the image name accordingly. |

---

#### Quick cheat‑sheet

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Force‑kill all VS Code windows |
| `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"` | List all VS Code processes and their PIDs |
| `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` | Force‑kill a specific VS Code instance |
| `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | PowerShell equivalent of the first command |
| `Stop-Process -Id <pid> -Force` | PowerShell equivalent of the second command |

Feel free to copy/paste the snippets into your command prompt or PowerShell window. Happy coding—and remember to save your work before you force‑quit!
